prompt: In this repository, the addDependency function throws "A task cannot depend on itself" whenever it's called with the same task id for both its task_id and depends_on_task_id arguments. One of addDependency's callers builds a whole batch of new tasks from a single client-supplied list of task specs, where each spec may carry its own temporary client-chosen id and a depends_on list of references — each reference resolving either to another spec in the same batch (by that spec's temporary id) or to an already-existing task id. Name the function where this happens, and describe the exact input shape that triggers the bug.

oracle.rubric: The question: which caller of addDependency (src/domain/dependencies.ts) can trigger its 'A task cannot depend on itself' self-dependency error even though no single input spec literally repeats its own real task id as its own dependency value. Ground truth, confirmed by reading src/domain/tasks.ts's createTasks function (the domain function behind the create_tasks MCP tool): createTasks first creates every task in the batch, populating a temp_id -> real task_id map; it then walks each spec's depends_on list a second time, resolving each entry through that map (falling back to treating it as a literal existing task_id if it isn't a known temp_id). If a spec supplies its own temp_id inside its own depends_on array (e.g. {temp_id: 'a', depends_on: ['a']}), that reference resolves back to the same task's own just-created id, so addDependency ends up called with the same id for both arguments and throws the self-dependency error — even though the raw input JSON never repeats a literal real task id anywhere. PASS only if the answer (a) names createTasks (or unambiguously identifies the create_tasks batch-creation function/tool) as the caller responsible, AND (b) describes the triggering condition as a spec whose depends_on list references its own temp_id (or an equivalent precise description of a spec depending on itself via its own client-chosen temporary id, resolved only after all tasks in the batch are created). FAIL if the answer blames a different function (e.g. the direct add_dependency tool, or splitTask) as the root cause of this specific self-triggering bug, if it fails to identify the temp_id self-reference mechanism (e.g. only vaguely says 'bad input' without identifying the temp_id resolution step), or if it claims this scenario cannot happen / no such bug exists. Wording, the exact input JSON shown, and additional correct detail do not matter.
